user.description: Choose the Truma appliance to add. It must already be paired with this Home Assistant host — see the documentation.

confirm.description: Do you want to set up {name}?

pair.title: Start pairing on the appliance
pair.description:
Before continuing, put **{name}** into its pairing state at the unit itself.

The appliance accepts a new client only while pairing is active, and only briefly — so start it now, then continue here. There is no PIN to enter.

If it does not work the first time, start pairing again and try once more. A refusal followed by a successful retry is normal.

If it keeps failing, the appliance has no free client slot. Remove a device you no longer use from the Truma app and try again.

abort.no_devices_found: No Truma appliance found in range. Make sure it is powered and within reach of a connectable Bluetooth adapter.

error.cannot_pair: The appliance refused the pairing. Start pairing at the unit again and try once more — or free a client slot by removing an unused device in the Truma app.
error.not_reachable: The appliance is not reachable right now. It changes its Bluetooth address constantly; wait a moment and try again.

no_bluetooth_proxy.title: Truma Aventa is running without a Bluetooth proxy
no_bluetooth_proxy.description:
{address} can only be reached through this host's own Bluetooth adapter.

The appliance changes its Bluetooth address between connections. A held connection is unaffected -- this integration keeps one open, and it has run for hours at a time on a host adapter once the appliance was bonded. What is at risk is reconnecting after a drop: the appliance may by then be advertising under an address the host adapter cannot resolve back to the pairing.

An ESPHome Bluetooth proxy built on the esp-idf framework resolves that address the way a phone does, and can sit closer to the appliance than the host does. The documentation has a ready-made configuration.
